title: Why use multiple threads

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Threads let a program do several things at once. A server handles many requests in parallel, so a slow database call doesn't block other users. Threads use multiple CPU cores for compute-heavy work. They also keep the interface responsive while background work runs. The cost is complexity: shared state needs care, and too many threads waste memory and cause contention. Use a bounded pool rather than one thread per task.

points.title: Parallel work
points.why: Multiple cores run threads at the same time, so the work finishes sooner.

points.title: Responsiveness
points.why: Blocking I/O in one thread doesn't stop the others.
